findings.finding: Revised MSME criteria notified via S.O. 1364(E) dated 21 Mar 2025, effective 1 Apr 2025. Medium: investment up to ₹125 Cr (was ₹50 Cr) and turnover up to ₹500 Cr (was ₹250 Cr). Small: ₹25 Cr / ₹100 Cr. Micro: ₹2.5 Cr / ₹10 Cr. Implication: 'medium enterprise' now covers ₹100–₹500 Cr turnover, i.e. the bottom half of Aroh's ICP band.
findings.figure: Medium = investment ≤ ₹125 Cr AND turnover ≤ ₹500 Cr (from 1 Apr 2025)
findings.source_title: Govt. Revises Investment and Turnover Criteria for Classifying Enterprises as MSMEs
findings.publisher: Taxmann (citing Ministry of MSME notification S.O. 1364(E)); corroborated by News On AIR (Prasar Bharati) 24 Mar 2025
findings.verified_how: fetched_page (Taxmann) + fetched_page (https://newsonair.gov.in/govt-notifies-revised-criteria-for-classifying-msmes, which states effect from 1 April)

findings.topic: Registered medium enterprises on Udyam — latest count
findings.finding: As of 31 Jul 2026, 9.16 crore MSMEs registered on Udyam + Udyam Assist; split 9,11,07,705 micro, 5,40,908 small and 41,722 medium (per Ministry reply reported by Kashmir Life). This SUPPORTS the source doc's 'roughly 42,000 registered medium enterprises' but the date should read 'as of 31 July 2026' (not October 2026) and the source should be the Ministry parliamentary reply rather than dashboard.msme.gov.in (dashboard could not be opened — TLS error).
findings.source_title: Jammu Kashmir Records Over 9.64 Lakh MSME Registrations Since 2020
findings.publisher: Kashmir Life (reporting Ministry of MSME reply in Parliament)
findings.tier: Tier 1 data via Tier 2/3 regional press
findings.verified_how: fetched_secondary — quote: '9,11,07,705 micro enterprises, 5,40,908 small enterprises and 41,722 medium enterprises'. Primary Rajya Sabha reply not opened.

findings.topic: Registered medium enterprises on Udyam — earlier data points (trend check)
findings.finding: Lok Sabha Unstarred Q 4822 (21 Aug 2025): from 01.07.2020 to 15.08.2025, 6.69 crore enterprises incl. IMEs on URP: Micro 6,64,49,516; Small 4,78,829; Medium 35,884. A June 2026 aggregation of the Ministry's district-wise Udyam dataset on data.gov.in gives 37,042 medium out of 4,71,55,579 (Udyam portal only). Series is consistent: ~35.9K (Aug 2025) → ~37.0K (Jun 2026, URP only) → 41.7K (Jul 2026, URP+UAP).
findings.source_title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 4822 (AU4822); India MSME Statistics 2026 (datarankindia.com); India MSME Udyam map 2026 (galific.com)
findings.publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat / Ministry of MSME; DataRank India and Galific (Tier 3 aggregators of data.gov.in)
findings.verified_how: Lok Sabha figure: search_snippet (eparlib refused connection). 37,042: fetched_secondary on both aggregator pages.

findings.finding: NITI Aayog 'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises' (May 2025) is reported as ~0.3% of registered MSMEs being medium; Drishti IAS summarises this as ~69,300 medium units on Udyam (Feb 2025) out of 5.93 crore. This is ~2x the Lok Sabha/Ministry figures (35,884 in Aug 2025; 41,722 in Jul 2026). Likely a different base/definition; prefer the Ministry figure. Do not use 0.3% × total registrations.
findings.figure: ~69,300 medium units (Feb 2025, per secondary summary) vs 35,884–41,722 (Ministry)
findings.source_title: Strengthening Medium Enterprises as a Catalyst for MSME Growth

findings.finding: Over 7.83 crore enterprises registered on Udyam Registration Portal + Udyam Assist Platform as of 28 Feb 2026 (IBEF, citing Ministry of MSME); 9.16 crore as of 31 Jul 2026 (Kashmir Life). No micro/small/medium split in IBEF article.
findings.source_title: Over 7.83 crore enterprises registered on Udyam platforms, indicating strong MSME formalisation growth

findings.topic: Indian entities by revenue band — ₹100–₹1,000 Cr and ₹1,000–₹5,000 Cr (BEST ICP MATCH)
findings.finding: Probe42 (MCA-filings-based) revenue range of all 25,88,128 active companies + LLPs (March 2026 edition): ₹100–₹1,000 Cr = 34,295 (1.3%); ₹1,000–₹5,000 Cr = 3,708 (0.1%); >₹5,000 Cr = 878; ₹50–₹100 Cr = 26,087 (1.0%); ₹10–₹50 Cr = 1,04,074 (4.0%). Newsletter text: 'There are 64,090 entities in India having revenue between Rs 50 cr and Rs 5,000 cr' and '1,69,042 entities have revenue more than Rs 10 cr'. ICP band ₹100–₹5,000 Cr = 34,295 + 3,708 = 38,003 legal entities. Caveat: counts legal entities (subsidiaries counted separately; LLPs included), not business groups; band ₹100–₹500 Cr vs ₹500–₹1,000 Cr split NOT available.
findings.source_title: The Probe42 Newsletter — March 2026
findings.publisher: Probe Information Services (Probe42), based on MCA filings
findings.tier: Tier 2 (commercial MCA data provider; no government equivalent found)
findings.verified_how: fetched_pdf_text (PDF downloaded, pypdf extraction; table layout garbled but totals cross-check: 26,087+34,295+3,708 = 64,090 as stated; 1,04,074+64,090+878 = 1,69,042 as stated)

findings.topic: Indian entities by revenue band — July 2026 update
findings.finding: Probe42 July 2026 edition (data as on 31-Jul-2026): 27,05,186 active entities; 'Entities with revenue up to ₹100 cr: 26,65,276'; 'Entities with revenue between ₹50 cr and ₹5,000 cr: 66,352'; 'Entities reporting revenue above ₹5,000 cr: 897'. Bands as % of active entities: 50–100: 1.0%; 100–1k: 1.3%; 1k–5k: 0.1%. Derived ICP (₹100–₹5,000 Cr) = 27,05,186 − 26,65,276 − 897 = 39,013 entities. Also: 19,21,599 private limited companies, 62,522 public limited non-govt companies, 5,15,722 LLPs; 7,269 non-government listed companies.
findings.source_title: The Probe Newsletter — July 2026

findings.finding: 27,05,186 active companies + LLPs as of 31 Jul 2026 out of 37,77,339 ever registered (Probe42). Instafinancials gives 21.17 lakh active companies (excluding LLPs) of 31.4 lakh registered as of 31 May 2026 (search snippet only). No official MCA 2026 figure retrieved.
findings.figure: 27.05 lakh active companies+LLPs (2026-07-31); ~21.2 lakh active companies excl. LLPs (2026-05-31, snippet)
findings.source_title: The Probe Newsletter — July 2026; India corporate landscape 2026 (Instafinancials blog)

findings.topic: Historical tax-return cross-check: companies above ₹250 Cr / ₹400 Cr turnover
findings.finding: Union Budget 2018-19 speech (as reported): of about 7 lakh companies filing returns, about 7,000 with turnover above ₹250 Cr (FY2016-17) remain in the 30% slab. Budget 2019-20: raising the 25% threshold to ₹400 Cr covers 99.3% of companies; 0.7% remain outside. Dated (FY17/FY18 data) and below today's Probe42 counts — use only as a floor/sanity check.
findings.figure: ~7,000 companies > ₹250 Cr turnover (FY2016-17); 0.7% of companies > ₹400 Cr (Budget 2019)
findings.source_title: Union Budget 2018-19 and 2019-20 speeches (as reported by PTI/Business Standard, Taxscan, others)
findings.verified_how: search_snippet (Business Standard and indiabudget.gov.in returned 403; Taxscan page fetched but did not contain the figures)

findings.topic: Sector mix of mid-sized companies (₹250–₹1,000 Cr and >₹1,000 Cr bands)
findings.finding: Probe42 top-5 industries by count per revenue band. Feb 2026 edition — ₹250–1,000 Cr: Metals & Minerals 1,471; Food & Beverages 1,243; Manufacturing 1,226; Automobiles 1,135; IT 968. ₹50–250 Cr: Manufacturing 5,862; Metals & Minerals 4,013; F&B 3,876; IT 3,275; Consumer Products 2,983. >₹1,000 Cr: BFSI 549; IT 452; F&B 426; Metals & Minerals 389; Manufacturing 382. May 2025 edition — ₹250–1,000 Cr: IT 1,590; Metals & Minerals 1,550; F&B 1,418; Manufacturing 1,360; Agro 1,291. Industrial/manufacturing categories (Metals, Manufacturing, Automobiles, F&B) dominate the mid band. Distribution/logistics and B2B services do NOT appear in any top-5; shares for those sectors NOT VERIFIED.
findings.figure: Top-5 industry counts per band (see finding); only top-5 published
findings.source_title: The Probe42 Newsletter — February 2026; The Probe42 Newsletter — May 2025
